delivery_contract.rule_summary: A set may be sampled, but its anchor must be selected first. Any chosen follow-up stays beside that anchor in source order. A replay question also carries its own replay clip while retaining the complete parent recording.

sets.topic_summary: A professor surveys EMDR as a treatment for psychological trauma, including its aims, mechanisms, limits, and possible benefits.

questions.prompt_summary: Identify the subject that best captures the lecture as a whole.

options.summary: A narrow technical definition of the treatment
A comparison among several therapy categories
A survey of multiple unconventional trauma treatments
The purpose and practical value of EMDR

answer.rationale_summary: Most of the lecture explains what EMDR does and why the professor considers it useful.

questions.prompt_summary: Choose the professor's intended meaning of processing a traumatic experience.

options.summary: Describing the technical operation of EMDR
Returning mentally to the event itself
Understanding the event from a healthier mental state
Discussing the painful event during EMDR

answer.rationale_summary: The lecture treats processing as healthier understanding, not merely remembering or describing an event.

questions.prompt_summary: Infer the professor's overall position toward EMDR.

options.summary: Positive about its distinct approach, evidence, and future
Convinced that psychologists still need substantial time to understand it
Uncertain whether the benefits last
Certain it will replace most other trauma treatment

answer.rationale_summary: Her examples and conclusion consistently frame the treatment as distinctive and effective without claiming it will replace every alternative.

questions.prompt_summary: Classify each treatment feature as belonging to EMDR or to other therapy.

rows.summary: Prioritises mental state rather than bodily response
Can take longer when several layers of trauma emerge
Uses side-to-side eye movement while following a light

answer.rationale_summary: The lecture contrasts the bodily element of EMDR with other therapy and explicitly assigns the layered-trauma delay and eye movement to EMDR.

questions.prompt_summary: Interpret the professor's metaphor about a traumatic memory becoming fixed in time.

options.summary: The original event seems to last unusually long
The unwanted memory remains present and persistent
Comparable events repeatedly occur in the person's life
The event only appears more disabling than it is

answer.rationale_summary: The metaphor refers to a memory that remains stuck and repeatedly returns, not to the event literally happening again.

questions.prompt_summary: Determine why the professor gives a caution about treatment speed and individual needs.

options.summary: To discourage rushing treatment merely for a fast result
To define EMDR as a strictly time-limited method
To argue that every other therapy is slower and weaker
To forbid EMDR with a newly met patient

answer.rationale_summary: Her point is that client needs matter more than speed, not that the treatment has a fixed duration or a blanket restriction.

sets.topic_summary: A student asks a professor how to turn an unfocused history lesson on Henry VIII into an engaging class presentation.

questions.prompt_summary: Identify the student's main reason for meeting the professor.

options.summary: To make a potentially dull lesson more engaging
To share recent personal and family news
To learn missing facts about English history
To complain about another instructor's assignment

answer.rationale_summary: After brief small talk, the student asks for help making a history lesson less dry.

questions.prompt_summary: Infer what the student's reference to three less-discussed English kings implies.

options.summary: Their reigns were too short to matter
Too little evidence survives to teach them well
Historians generally dislike them
Students tend to know them less well than Henry VIII

answer.rationale_summary: The comparison concerns how much students learn about those rulers, not their merit, reign length, or historical record.

questions.prompt_summary: Choose the claim that reflects the student's view of Henry VIII.

options.summary: His vivid personality is a major reason people remember him
Stories about his life are usually exaggerated
Executing his wives proves he was cruel
His legacy still directly controls European politics

answer.rationale_summary: The student describes striking biographical details and treats Henry as a memorable, larger-than-life figure.

questions.prompt_summary: Identify what the student proposes doing before teaching the lesson.

options.summary: Review the plan with a different professor
Rehearse the lecture to improve the storytelling
Find additional dramatic facts about Henry
Listen to a peer teach the same material

answer.rationale_summary: Near the end, the student suggests trying the lecture on someone first so the story can be delivered better.

questions.prompt_summary: Interpret why the professor reassures the student during the replayed exchange.

options.summary: She considers the other professor unfairly intimidating
She believes the student's concern is unfounded
She invites the student to ask for guidance comfortably
She offers to help teach the lesson herself

answer.rationale_summary: The reassurance opens space for the student to explain the problem and seek advice; it is not an offer to co-teach.
